guide.title: Spinal Motion Restriction Skills
guide.lead: Decide by assessment, not by mechanism alone. Patients who need it get a collar and a flat, padded, well-fitted surface – a scoop or vacuum mattress, not a long board for the ride. Patients who don't need it are better off without it.

sections.title: Spinal motion restriction (blunt trauma)
include: Distracting injury or circumstances (including children who can't be assessed)
exclude: Alert, sober, no midline pain or tenderness, normal neuro exam, no distracting injury (NEXUS)
Penetrating trauma without neuro deficit: no spinal immobilisation

steps.title: Manual stabilisation
steps.text: Hold the head in line from the start.

steps.title: Collar
steps.text: Size from the top of the shoulder (trapezius) to the angle of the jaw; neutral position.

steps.title: Ambulatory patient
steps.text: Collar on, let them step and sit onto the stretcher; no board.

steps.title: Log roll
steps.text: At least 4 people: one at the head calls the moves; minimise rolls (a scoop needs none).

steps.title: Secure
steps.text: Pad gaps; straps torso first (chest then pelvis), then head, then legs. Recheck neuro.

steps.title: Breathing worse?
steps.text: Loosen chest straps; tilt the whole board for vomiting; sit up if safe.

sections.title: Special cases
rows: Pad under the shoulders: the large head flexes the neck
Pad to their shape; don't force them flat; collar may not fit – use towels
Tilt the whole board to the left, or wedge under the right hip
Child in an intact car seat
May transport in the seat if it fits the stretcher and the child is stable
Unsafe scene or arrest in a car
Rapid extrication with as much alignment as possible

quiz.q: Restrained driver, low-speed rear-end, GCS 15, no midline tenderness, normal neuro, sober, no distracting injury. Motion restriction?
options: None needed: document and transport sitting if wanted

quiz.q: Which mechanism alone requires spinal motion restriction?
78-year-old after a ground-level fall: neck pain with midline tenderness, normal neuro. Best transport?
options: Collar (or padding) and secured on the stretcher in a comfortable position, padded to her shape
No restriction: older people are harmed by boards
quiz.explanation: Older adults fracture with low energy.

quiz.q: Patient on a board becomes short of breath. You:
options: Loosen chest straps; if no better, move to a scoop or vacuum mattress and sit up if safe

quiz.explanation: Also no intoxication, no focal deficit.

options: Trapezius to the angle of the jaw

quiz.q: Minimum crew for a log roll:
Children under about 8 on a flat surface need:
Stab wound to the neck, normal neuro. Collar?
options: No: penetrating trauma without deficit doesn't need immobilisation
quiz.explanation: Collars hide bleeding and airway problems.

quiz.q: Best surface for transport when restriction is needed:

flashcards.question: NEXUS criteria
flashcards.answer: No posterior midline tenderness, no focal neuro deficit, normal alertness, no intoxication, no distracting injury.

flashcards.question: What a collar does
flashcards.answer: Limits movement only partly and reminds the patient not to move; it's not a substitute for a good surface and padding.

flashcards.question: Collar sizing
flashcards.answer: From the top of the shoulder (trapezius) to the angle of the jaw, with the neck neutral.

flashcards.question: Log roll crew
flashcards.answer: At least 4: one at the head calling the moves, three at the body. Scoops avoid rolling.

flashcards.question: Rapid extrication
flashcards.answer: Unsafe scene, cardiac arrest, or a patient who needs immediate life-saving care.

flashcards.question: Children under about 8
flashcards.answer: Large occiput flexes the neck on a flat surface: pad under the shoulders. Pediatric collar.

flashcards.question: Pregnancy over 20 weeks
flashcards.answer: Tilt the whole board left or wedge under the right hip to prevent supine hypotension.

flashcards.question: Securing order
flashcards.answer: Pad gaps, torso first (chest then pelvis), then head, then legs. Recheck neuro after.

critical.scenario: High-speed side impact: driver's door crushed, fuel leaking. Driver alert, no spine pain, normal neuro, but a deformed femur.
critical.question: Sequence?

options.t: Rapid extrication for the fuel hazard with manual alignment; the femur is a distracting injury so restrict motion (collar, scoop or vacuum), then splint
Full careful extrication with a short board first
Splint the femur in the car first

critical.explanation: Scene hazards decide the speed; findings decide restriction.
critical.kpi: Applies rapid extrication and NEXUS correctly

critical.scenario: Fall of 4 m onto his feet: both heels very painful, no spine pain, normal neuro, sober, GCS 15.
critical.question: Motion restriction?

options.t: Yes: painful heel fractures are distracting injuries and axial loading often fractures the lumbar spine

critical.explanation: Scoop or vacuum mattress; splint the heels.
critical.kpi: Recognizes distracting injuries in axial-load mechanisms

critical.scenario: 5-year-old in an intact car seat after a moderate rear-end crash: crying but consolable, no tenderness, moves everything.
critical.question: Best approach?

options.t: No restriction needed if the exam is reliable; transport in the car seat secured to the stretcher and explain to the parents
Board and collar always for children
Remove him from the seat onto a board

critical.explanation: If the child can't be assessed reliably, restrict in the seat with padding.
critical.kpi: Applies selective spinal motion restriction in children
